summary: Lewis County, WA ground-level lookout cab in Gifford Pinchot NF: built 1929 per most sources, abandoned in the 1960s, listed gone; neighbouring trail open to the public.

facts.design: Ground-level lookout cab (FFLOS listing type 'Ground'); built 1929 per most sources; Firelookout.com lists an L-4 cab in 1938
facts.status_note: FFLOS listing marks the site Gone; sources say the lookout was abandoned in the 1960s; the Forest Service describes phone-line sections still along Trail 109; no source describes the cab as it stands today

access.note: Gifford Pinchot National Forest; the Forest Service says the nearby Trail 109 is open to motorcycles, hikers, horses and bicycles; no closure for the lookout site found

visit.drive_up: Gravel road passable for most cars per WillhiteWeb, which calls the road deteriorating quickly (page undated)
visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb: 1 to 1.5 miles one-way, 300 to 850 feet of elevation gain; Forest Service says Hamilton Ridge Trail 109A connects Trail 109 with Hamilton Buttes Trail 118

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest (FFLOS: administered by U.S. Forest Service)

events.note: Cab built in the summer of 1929 (WillhiteWeb); Forest Service says the lookout was built in 1929; June 1929 newspapers reported plans to erect a tower there in July and August
Firelookout.com lists an L-4 cab in 1938
Registered December 12, 2013 as FFLOS US 1544, WA 439; nominated by Rob Jeter

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 5,676 ft (1,730 m); Firelookout.com (5772') and WillhiteWeb (5,772 feet) give 5,772 ft. The brief's 1730 m matches the register. The story gives both figures and does not pick one.

Forest Service and WillhiteWeb date the cab to 1929, and June 1929 newspapers reported planned tower construction that summer. Firelookout.com alone lists a cab in 1924. The story gives the 1929 date as the majority reading and reports the 1924 claim with its source.

The FFLOS listing types the site as Ground, and Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb call it a cab. The 1929 newspaper reports planned towers. The story describes a lookout cab and does not say a tower was built.

notes_for_editor: Six sources; the Forest Service page is the only official one. Early dates conflict (1924 cab per Firelookout.com vs 1929 elsewhere). Staffing is only implied by the abandonment date. The 1938 'L-4 cab' is the Firelookout.com reading only. The 1929 newspaper items name a planned tower that no source says was built. Photos seen but not captured: FFLOS shows 1929 panoramas credited to the National Archives Pacific Northwest Region and a photo from the Ron Kemnow collection; no direct URLs were captured, so none is listed. The cab's current condition is not described anywhere; the phone-line remnant is on Trail 109.
